Question Text: A cart travels 15 m in 5 s. Calculate its average speed and include units.
Answer 1: 3 m/s

Question Text: During a 12-minute bicycle trip, the rider’s average speed is 8 m/s. At one instant, the speedometer reads 11 m/s. Distinguish the two measurements.
Answer 1: 8 m/s describes the whole trip average; 11 m/s is the instantaneous speed at that moment.
Answer 4: The larger value must be velocity because it is larger.

Question Text: A robot moves at a steady 10 m/s south. Explain what makes this a velocity description rather than only a speed description, and state what would make the velocity change even if the speed stayed 10 m/s.
Answer 1: It gives both speed (10 m/s) and direction (south). The velocity changes if the direction changes, even if the speed remains 10 m/s.
Answer 2: Velocity is only the number on a speedometer.
Answer 3: Velocity changes only when speed changes.
